I will get to that shortly. I wanted to jump ahead to the Confirmation andle (CC).

While we call this the CE pattern in part because it was already called that, we mainly call this the CE pattern because the Entry signal Confirms what the pattern signifies. Ultimately, our pattern is thought to represent a change in the Supply/Demand Dynamic in the market. At the heart of this change, is either the emand wamping upply DSS) inverval or the Supply wamping emand (SSD) interval.

The CC:

1. For a long, the CC must close higher than the previous candle. And for a short, the CC must close lower than the previous candle. 2. The body (ABS(Open-Close)) of the CC must be larger than the body (ABS(Open-Close)) of the previous candle. Where, ABS stands for absolute value. 3. For a long, the close of the CC must be greater than the midpoint of the Long Shadow of the DSS interval. For a short, the close of the CC must be less than the midpoint of the Long Shadow of the SSD interval.

Note: Based on the above rules, the CC can be the same interval as the SSD/DSS interval.

4. Progression. The maximum number of intervals that can appear after the SSD/DSS interval and the CC interval is three (3). Which is to say, if the SSD/DSS interval is not also the CC interval, the CC interval must occur within 4 intervals.

This shows the "full" progression of the CC interval. While I did not mention the NC, you can see a White (Open<Close) WRB among the intervals after the SSD. But it does not close above the high of the SSD's Long Shadow. Also note that this CE did not occur in a Zone, but it does create a Zone.

akifusenet wrote:...Here is a close up look at the pattern.

The DSS candle must: (1) have a low lower than the lows of the prior three (3) intervals. (2) The long Lower Shadow of the DSS candle, must be larger than the combination of its Upper Shadow and its body(Open-Close) (3) The DSS must appear 1-4 intervals after the appearance of a Dark BreakOut WRB Therefore, there can be 3 intervals after the Dark BreakOut WRB before we see the DSS (4) The Long Lower Shadow of the DSS candle must be greater than both the lower shadows and the bodies of all the intervals after the Dark BreakOut WRB (5) The Long Lower Shadow of the DSS candle must be greater than the lower shadow of the Dark BreakOut WRB (6) The Long Lower Shadow of the DSS candle must be greater than both the lower shadows and the bodies of the 3 intervals Prior to the Dark BreakOut WRB

The Long Lower Shadow of the DSS interval should be larger than the lower shadows of all intervals involved in the pattern that occur prior to the appearance of the DSS candle. The Long Lower Shadow should also be larger than the bodies (open-close) of all intervals involved in the pattern except the Dark BreakOut WRB. These tell us that the Long Lower Shadow does potentially represent a change in the Supply/Demand Dynamic in the market. Which is why we refer to it as a emand wamping upply DSS) candle.

I have mentioned this before, but it is worth repeating. The CE works best as a visual entry signal. That is to say, when you can look at a chart and visually determine all the rules are present, the signal tends to work better than if you have to do the math to determine if the rules are met. This visual nature is a benefit as one goes down in time frames. The lower the time frame, the less time one has to do the calculations. It also is beneficial if one is trading multiple markets. What signal should be taken? The signal that is visually apparent rather than the signal that needs to be calculated.

Yes.

The DSS candle must:

(1) have a low lower than the lows of the prior 3 intervals. (2) The long Lower Shadow of the DSS candle, must be larger than the combination of its Upper shadow and its body. (3) The DSS must appear 1-4 intervals after the appearance of a dark breakout WRB. Therefore, there can be 3 intervals after the dark breakout WRB before we see the DSS. (4) The long Lower Shadow of the DSS candle must be greater than the lower shadows of all the intervals after the dark breakout WRB. (5) The long Lower Shadow of the DSS candle must be greater than both the lower shadows and the bodies of the 3 intervals Prior to the dark breakout WRB. Akif, 

The DSS candle must: (1) have a low lower than the lows of the prior three (3) intervals. (2) The long Lower Shadow of the DSS candle, must be larger than the combination of its Upper Shadow and its body(Open-Close) (3) The DSS must appear 1-4 intervals after the appearance of a Dark BreakOut WRB Therefore, there can be 3 intervals after the Dark BreakOut WRB before we see the DSS (4) The Long Lower Shadow of the DSS candle must be greater than both the lower shadows and the bodies of all the intervals after the Dark BreakOut WRB (5) The Long Lower Shadow of the DSS candle must be greater than the lower shadow of the Dark BreakOut WRB (6) The Long Lower Shadow of the DSS candle must be greater than both the lower shadows and the bodies of the 3 intervals Prior to the Dark BreakOut WRB (7) The body of the DSS candle must be smaller than at least one of the bodies of the three (3) intervals prior to the Dark BreakOut WRB (7b) There must be at least one dark body (open>close) amongst the bodies of the three (3) intervals prior to the Dark BreakOut WRB

Note: While the Dark BreakOut WRB changes to White BreakOut WRB for shorts, the requirement of 1 dark interval among the prior three (3) remains dark for shorts.

At some point in our discovery, we talked about Progression of the start point (now called SSD/DSS).

While this is an INVALID signal, it is a great example of progression with the SSD interval. Why is it invalid? It is invalid because there is no dark interval among the three (3) intervals prior to the Dark WRB. I have shaded one of the intervals yellow to simulate a dark interval, so we can think of the pattern as valid.

Notice at SSD' we have "valid" signal. Again, it is not actually valid, as there is no dark interval among the three (3) intervals prior to the Dark WRB. But we are pretending that the shaded yellow candle is a dark (close>open) interval.

After we see SSD', our thoughts go to finding the CC by the next 4 intervals. While it is not a rule, we would like to see our CC close lower than the close of our SSD' interval. (The actual rule only requires it to close lower than the midpoint of the Long Shadow (LS) of the SSD interval)

The next interval turns out to be a SSD interval itself.

1. Its high is greater than the high of the privous three (3) intervals. 2. Its Long Upper Shadow is greater than the combination of its lower shadow and its body. 3. Its Long Upper Shadow is greater than the upper shadows of all the intervals in the pattern, including the upper shadow of the White WRB 4. Its Long Upper Shadow is greater than the bodies of all intervals in the pattern, excluding the White WRB 5. Its body is smaller than the body of at least one (1) interval of the three (3) intervals prior to the White WRB 6. There are no more than three (3) intervals after the appearance of the White WRB and the appearance of the SSD interval. **Note**: this rule does not need to be true for the progression. Only the firstSSD interval must meet this requirement.

After we see this new SSD interval, we would now begin looking for the CC interval again. Our "count" is set back to zero. Again, notice two intervals later when the CC does appear, it closes lower than the close of the SSD

Also keep in mind that this progression requires the new SSD/DSS intervals to be consecutive, or back to back.

Yes, I too think it is evolving nicely.

That's a great question about the rationale behind the dark body interval requirement.

It is true that the overall concept behind the CE entry could be described as, "a signal pattern manifested by a change in the Supply/Demand Dynamic", with three (3) intervals in particular, the Dark/White WRB, the SSD/DSS, and the CC being necessary elements of that change.

The rationale behind the dark body interval is much more utilitarian.

In looking at many successful CE pattern signals, I have found the that the vast majority of them have at least one dark interval among the three(3) intervals prior to the Dark/White WRB. This of course does not mean the existence of a dark interval guarantees a "winning" pattern. Which brings me to the next point. Among those patterns that "fail", I have noticed more of them do not have a dark interval among the three (3) intervals prior to the Dark/White WRB

There is another reason, which I touched on briefly when this project began. Take a look at the chart below.

This is one of my favorite types of CE entry. The DSS interval appears immediately after the Dark WRB, and the CC interval appears directly after the DSS interval. The DSS interval also happens to be a Doji. What we also have here is a valid "High Close Doji pattern". One of the requirements of the "High Close Doji Pattern", is a dark interval with its close higher than the close of the Doji, So by simply incorporating the need for a dark interval among the three(3) intervals prior to the Dark WRB, I have increased the possibility that a valid "High Close Doji Pattern" would be picked up. Therefore, instead of looking for both the CE entry and the "High Close Doji Pattern", I can focus on the CE entry. With the knowledge that most valid "High Close Doji Pattern signals will also be CE entry signals.

I wanted the CE to be broad enough to encompass a wide range of Price Action and yet be specific enough to incorporate some already known reliable Long Shadow family subgroups.
